title: Keeping the tills moving as the shop grows
target: How the checkout changes in Supermarket Simulator as the shop gets busier: serving the queue yourself, moving a till rather than rebuilding it, hiring cashiers as cashiers, and adding a self-checkout that has rules and can need repairs.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is open with at least one checkout placed
Some money for a till or a hire if you are adding one
A queue you can watch while you work

steps.do: Expect the end of a sale to be a step of its own rather than something that happens on its own.
steps.because: finishing a checkout is separate from the act of scanning, which is what lets a served customer leave and the next one step up (FinishCheckout)

steps.do: Move a checkout position rather than taking the lane apart when the layout changes.
steps.because: a checkout position can be picked up and moved on its own, so the layout is adjustable without rebuilding the till (MoveCheckoutPosition)

steps.do: Hire a cashier as a cashier rather than as general help.
steps.because: a cashier is its own kind of worker with its own hiring information, and cashier items exist separately from the checkout machine (Cashier, CashierSO, CashierItem)

steps.do: Let the cashier take the checkout over rather than trying to serve alongside them.
steps.because: there is a starting step for a cashier-run checkout that is distinct from you scanning at it (StartCashierCheckout)

steps.do: Check that a self-checkout can be used at all before you rely on it for a queue.
steps.because: the game tests whether the automated machine may be used rather than treating it as an ordinary lane (AutomatedCheckout, CanSelfCheckoutUsable)

steps.do: Do not walk away from a working self-checkout; wanting help is a separate question from working.
steps.because: whether a customer wants assistance is tracked apart from whether the machine functions (IsSelfCheckoutWantHelp)

steps.do: Watch whether anyone is actually at the till instead of guessing from the queue.
steps.because: the game keeps track of whether a customer is present at the checkout, which is what the rest of the lane reacts to (HasCheckoutCustomer)

steps.do: Expect the machines to be drawn in less detail as they get further away.
steps.because: a checkout carries a renderer whose job is to decide how much of it to draw, which is how several tills can stand in one shop (LODCheckoutRenderer)

steps.do: Treat a broken self-checkout as a repair job rather than a replacement.
steps.because: the game has its own handling for repairing an automated checkout (RepairingSelfCheckout)

steps.do: In a shared shop, expect the tills to be kept in step with the manager rather than each player's screen.
steps.because: the checkout and its automated version have networked forms and a networked manager behind them (NetworkCheckout, NetworkAutomatedCheckout, NetworkCheckoutManager)

steps.do: Remember the machine is one kind of checkout rather than a system apart.
steps.because: a checkout carries a type, and the automated machine is one of those types (CheckoutType)

commonMistakes: Treating a self-checkout as an ordinary staffed lane.
Assuming a working machine cannot still want help.
Taking a till apart when its position could simply be moved.
Hiring general helpers when the queue needs cashiers.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
